caption: A battery-powered toy car slows and stops as its battery runs flat, and its headlights dim and go out.

sa.check: A toy car drives along with its headlights lit.
The headlights dim and go out.
The car is battery powered: no cord or track feeds it.
The lights dim before they go out.
Moving and lit comes first, slowing and dimming follow, and the car is stopped and dark at the end.

pc.expect: The headlights dim as the car slows and go out around the time it stops; the two fade together.
pc.fail: The car stops while the headlights stay at full brightness to the end of the clip; or the lights go out while the car drives on to the end of the clip; or the lights go out well before the car begins to slow.

pc.expect: Slowing, stopping and dimming run one way: the car does not speed up or move again, and the lights do not brighten or come back.
pc.fail: The car speeds up again after slowing; or moves off again after stopping with nothing touching it; or the headlights come back on after going out; or the lights brighten as the car slows.

pc.expect: The car rolls on its wheels along the surface in the direction it faces; its wheels turn while it moves and stop when it stops.
pc.fail: The car slides sideways or drifts with its wheels still; or the wheels keep turning after the body has stopped; or the car lifts off the surface as it slows.

pc.expect: Nothing else on the floor moves when the car slows and stops.
pc.fail: Objects nearby shift as the car stops; or the car rocks or slides after halting with nothing touching it; or the rug slides beneath it.

pc.expect: One toy car with its wheels and lights attached; it stays on the surface and passes through nothing.
pc.fail: The car vanishes or a second car appears; or a wheel detaches or a headlight vanishes rather than going dark; or the car passes through a piece of furniture or a wall; or it changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The car's colour and markings and the floor stay the same apart from the lights.
pc.fail: The car changes colour; or its decals change; or the floor pattern changes.

note: The car is a powered toy: its slowing and stopping are the caption's event, not causeless motion. How quickly it slows is not judged.
